verified_scope: Exact native reception of raw auxiliary high nibbles, how a drum retrigger's repeats take voices and whether they overlap, and the remaining melodic lengths; predictions that failed are kept as failed

predictions.reception: The backup equals the compiled target exactly (every packet and the whole body), every auxiliary byte and effect included

H1_one_voice.statement: A drum note's repeats re-strike one voice: the retrigger of 4 plays all 4 onsets whether 0, 1, 2 or 3 other voices are held

H2_voice_per_repeat.statement: Each repeat needs a voice of its own and, like any new note, is dropped when none is free (a sounding note is never cut): with 0, 1, 2, 3 voices held the retrigger of 4 plays 4, 3, 2, 1 onsets

H1_restart.statement: A repeat cuts the previous one and restarts the sample: the body power 12 to 52 ms after the fourth onset of the unaccompanied retrigger equals the single hit's after its onset (0 dB, within 1.5 dB)

H2_overlap.statement: Repeats overlap and their bodies add in power: after the fourth onset the body power is the single hit's summed at offsets 0, 62.5, 125 and 187.5 ms (predicted from the reference hit, about +4 dB), within 1.5 dB; undecided if that prediction is under 3 dB

H_holders_continue.statement: No holder is cut by the drum: every holder sounds its full eight steps (2.0 s, within 60 ms), as a sounding note is never cut (voice-steal-results.md)

H_length_steps.statement: A melodic note with high nibble n in 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, A, B, C, D, E sounds for n steps (250 ms each, within 60 ms)

H_F_15_steps.statement: Nibble F is fifteen steps like the others: 3.75 s (within 60 ms) of the 5 s tone

H_F_whole_sample.statement: Nibble F plays the whole sample: the 5 s tone sounds 5.0 s (within 100 ms)

session_answers.question: Pattern 1, second half, and Patterns 2 to 4 (the drum with low tones): did the drum burst sound the same in every bar, or thinner as more tones played? (notes)
Patterns 9 to 14 (two steady tones per bar, then one): did the tones stop at different times? (notes)

limits: One session on one device, at 60 BPM with no swing (aux-nibble-003 covers tempo and swing)
Onset counting assumes repeats at least 10 ms apart; the closest here are 62.5 ms
The choke reading assumes the body's noise adds in power when copies overlap; a restart that did not reset the sample's start would read as neither
